sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Software architecture interview questions cover the higher-level patterns senior interviews probe — layered vs hexagonal vs clean architecture, DDD (entities, aggregates, bounded contexts, ubiquitous language), CQRS and event sourcing, the SOLID principles applied at the system level, modular monolith vs microservices, and the architectural trade-offs interviewers love to discuss (consistency vs availability, cohesion vs coupling). Use this page for staff/principal-level interviews where the question is rarely "how would you implement X" and more often "how would you decompose Y".

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Four lenses for any architecture question:

- **Layered** — easy, but couples to data model.
- **Hexagonal / Ports & Adapters** — domain in the middle, infra on the edges.
- **Clean** — concentric layers, dependency rule points inward.
- **DDD** — bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language.

Pick the **lightest** that solves the problem. Senior signal = articulate trade-offs.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Architectural styles** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Clean architecture** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Cqrs and event sourcing** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Domain driven design** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Hexagonal architecture** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Microservices patterns** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **DDD aggregates** — one transactional boundary, identity by ID, rules inside.
- **CQRS** — different models for read and write; events keep them in sync.
- **Modular monolith** — the underrated default; 95% of teams don't need microservices.
- **Conway's law** — architecture mirrors org structure.
- **Reversible vs one-way doors** — invest the most thought in one-way doors (data model, public APIs).

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd start with a modular monolith using hexagonal boundaries, isolate the domain from infra, draw <bounded contexts> with explicit integration patterns, and only split into services when <independent deploy / scale / team boundary> demands it."*
